documents.title: Generative AI Policy (Policy 312)
documents.summary: A short IT-governance policy, owned by the Center for Learning and Teaching, that supports responsible GenAI use by faculty, staff and students. It sets five principles: protect data, disclose use, uphold integrity, verify output and keep human oversight. It gives no course-level rules.
documents.stance_why: The policy says the university "supports the responsible use" of GenAI and that "the use of AI tools is encouraged", but attaches conditions on disclosure, privacy approval, integrity and verification. It is a campus-wide permission with conditions, not a delegation to instructors or a ban, so permit.

units.why: The opening sentence sets the institution's purpose: the university "supports the responsible use" of GenAI for teaching, learning, research and administration. It is a campus-wide framework statement, so P56 fits better than P02, since it states support in principle rather than a default rule for coursework.

documents.title: Gen AI and Your Syllabus (sample syllabus statements)
tiers: Can use generative AI in certain instances or specific ways
documents.summary: The teaching center offers sample syllabus statements in three groups: AI allowed, AI allowed in limited ways, and AI prohibited. Instructors choose and adapt one, explain why, and add reminders to verify output and avoid personal data.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule for the university: it says some instructors may "allow, or even encourage" AI and others "prohibit" it, and offers statements that "might be used, combined, or adapted". It sorts them into three groups, so it delegates and lists them as tiers.

units.why: The page opens by saying some instructors "may want to allow, or even encourage" AI and others "prohibit" it. The decision is left to each instructor, so P04.

units.why: The suggested statements are meant to "shape the message you provide to your students on a course syllabus and/or on assignment instructions". It recommends putting expectations in the syllabus; P09 fits, with a soft modality as these are only suggestions.
